description: Full-inference kernel census of an Orin-built INT8-quantized VAD-Base head engine (real-data PTQ calibration; MatMul/Softmax kept FP16 by design) on AGX Orin. One profiled inference (torch.cuda.profiler start/stop around a single trt_run), captured with Nsight Compute 2024.3.1 (--set basic, --profile-from-start off, --clock-control none). Finding: ZERO INT8/IMMA kernels execute; INT8 never touches the dominant kernels.

meta.engine: Orin-built INT8-quantized VAD-Base head engine (real-data PTQ calibration; MatMul/Softmax kept FP16)
meta.honesty_note: ncu serializes kernels and flushes caches per replay, so absolute per-kernel times are inflated ~2x vs the 291.5 ms CUDA-event wall time at MAXN. Category SHARES are the meaningful output; do not cite the absolute ms.

top_kernels.name: ms_deformable_im2col_gpu_kernel_opt8
top_kernels.note: MSDeformAttn plugin, __half vectorized; SM 64%/Mem 65% = latency/occupancy-bound (gather-heavy), neither pipe saturated

top_kernels.name: __myl_CasMulCasSum / ResMulResAdd / ResCasMaxSubExpSumDiv / Cas / ... (TRT fused elementwise)
top_kernels.note: attention/FFN plumbing fused by TRT; SM 17%/Mem 57%

conclusion: The INT8-quantized head engine runs 100% FP16 kernels. INT8-eligible ops (conv) are ~0% of head time; MatMuls are deliberately FP16; the deform plugin has no INT8 implementation. INT8's 2x arithmetic advantage therefore has no dominant kernel to accelerate.
